data.title: Pet ownership and cognitive functioning in later adulthood across pet types
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章研究了宠物饲养与晚年认知功能之间的关系，特别是不同类型的宠物（如狗、猫、鸟、鱼）以及不同年龄组对认知衰退的影响。通过分析欧洲健康与退休调查的数据，研究发现饲养宠物与认知功能（执行功能和情景记忆）的衰退减缓相关。具体来说，狗和猫的饲养与较慢的认知衰退有关，而鸟和鱼则没有这种关联。年龄组并未显著影响这种关系。研究表明，饲养狗和猫可能有助于减缓认知衰退，支持健康的认知老化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：养宠物（尤其是狗）对心理健康、社交互动和认知功能的影响

不同观点：
• **thenaturalist**：认为养狗带来了显著的心理和社交好处，特别是在缓解压力和增加与陌生人互动方面。他以自身经历说明养狗帮助他管理ADHD症状，并通过观察狗的行为学会了处理错误和再次尝试的积极态度。

• **ludicrousdispla**：关注评论中的科学表达问题，指出科学出版物中图表标注不清晰的问题，强调图表信息应完整描述。这表明其关注点在于科学表达的准确性，而非养狗本身的影响。

• **cainxinth**：认为狗带来的心理健康改善可能部分源于身体锻炼，提出照顾宠物（尤其是狗或猫）的老年人由于需要更多活动，可能在身体和大脑健康上获益更多。

• **montroser**：质疑养狗与认知功能改善之间的因果关系，认为可能是认知能力较强的人更倾向于养狗，而非养狗导致认知能力改善。提出需要更多证据来证明因果关系。

• **bestouff**：引用研究结果指出，狗和猫的饲养与认知能力下降较慢有关，而鸟类和鱼类则没有类似关联，表明宠物类型可能对健康影响不同。

• **torbid**：对鸟类与猫狗的比较提出疑问，认为可能存在隐藏变量，如养狗或猫可能需要更多居住许可，从而影响结果。

• **luqtas**：希望看到更多控制变量（如爱好和社会活动）的研究，认为仅看居住情况（独自生活或与他人同住）并不能充分解释认知益处。

• **tmaier**：关注照顾孙辈对老年人认知功能的影响，提出类似养宠物可能带来的益处，扩展讨论范围至其他类型的责任性活动。

补充讨论：
- 养狗对心理健康和社交互动的具体机制尚不完全清楚，但可能与锻炼、情绪调节和社交机会增加有关。
- 讨论中对研究设计和因果关系的质疑，强调了进一步研究和变量控制的必要性。
- 不同类型宠物的比较以及居住情况、活动参与等因素对认知功能的影响也是讨论中的重要方面。

44474894.article_content:
Longitudinal relationships between pet ownership and cognitive functioning in later adulthood across pet types and individuals’ ages
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Human behaviour
Psychology
Abstract
Pet ownership has been shown to have a positive influence on cognitive functioning and cognitive decline in late adulthood. However, there is limited understanding of how different species of pets are associated with these outcomes in different age groups. This study employed a multilevel modelling approach using data from eight waves of the Survey of Health and Retirement in Europe (SHARE) to longitudinally examine: (1) the relationship between pet ownership and cognitive decline over 18 years among adults aged 50 and older, (2) The moderating role of younger vs. older age subgroups on this relationship, and (3) the distinct role of owning dogs, cats, birds, and fish. The targeted cognitive domains were executive functioning and episodic memory. Results confirmed that pet ownership is associated with slower decline in both cognitive domains. While age group did not moderate this relationship, differences emerged in the relationship between cognitive decline and individual pet species. Dog and cat ownership was associated with slower cognitive decline compared to no pet ownership; bird and fish ownership showed no such association. These findings suggest that dog and cat ownership might act as a protective factor aiding to slow down cognitive decline, thus contributing to healthy cognitive ageing.

Introduction
Age-related cognitive decline is an increasingly pressing concern in public health, which may begin in early adulthood and accelerate with increasing age

. While much research is still investigating the precise mechanisms of cognitive ageing, previous studies have identified several contributing factors, including for example genetics, general health and lifestyle choices

7
. Cognitive decline is a major public health concern on both individual and societal levels due to its association with diminished well-being and health-related quality of life
8
,
9
as well as increased caregiving burden
10
and health- and long-term care costs
11
. Therefore, it is important to investigate potential avenues to support cognitive health across the lifespan.
With regards to individual lifestyle factors, previous research has shown that, for example, an adherence to a Mediterranean- or DASH-style diet rich in vegetables, fruits, whole grains and unsaturated fats; sleeping 7–8 h per night with limited night-time fragmentation; regular participation in social clubs or volunteering; enrolment in adult-education courses; or employment in cognitively demanding occupations, are related to reduced or delayed deterioration of cognitive functioning
12
,
13
,
14
. Another potentially protective factor of cognitive health, which has received so far relatively little attention, is pet ownership. Approximately 38% of Europeans own pets, with similar rates of pet ownership estimated in older adults aged 50 and above
14
,
15
,
16
,
17
.
Numerous studies have linked pet ownership to a range of physical and mental health benefits
18
,
19
,
20
. When it comes to pet ownership in later age specifically, it has been shown to have a positive effect on older adults’ well-being and feelings of companionship
19
as well as on their physical health. A systematic review by Gee and Mueller
20
found robust evidence linking pet ownership to better physical health, in particular, cardiac health and physiological responses to stress, such as lower blood pressure or lower risk of fatal cardiac events in patients with hypertension. Furthermore, the review revealed that pet ownership had important psychosocial benefits. Specifically, older pet owners perceived lower rates of loneliness, and dog ownership in particular was linked to increased physical activity, which in turn related to positive social outcomes.
A further systematic review by Hughes and colleagues
21
similarly concluded that human-animal interactions can benefit older adults’ physical but also mental health, including improvements in their quality of life and levels of depression and anxiety. data.title: Optimizing Tool Selection for LLM Workflows with Differentiable Programming
data.author: viksit
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在工具调用、上下文管理和成本效率优化中的应用及挑战

不同观点：
• bigmadshoe认为，在早期的代理工作流中，对上下文进行高度修饰以提供简化的表示是标准做法，并强调了每个LLM调用会增加延迟、成本和token开销，且会累积上下文负担。
• viksit介绍了通过本地可学习路由器减少token开销和成本的实验，并发布了相关文章，提出使用PyTorch基础学习器来委托工具调用，并欢迎反馈。
• pcwelder对viksit的方法提出质疑，认为其本质上是在训练自己的语言模型，而不是使用预训练的大型LM，并指出在非关键任务中使用较小的LM可能会降低准确性。
• Garlef质疑选择是否真的是问题所在，认为需要根据上下文确定工具的有效载荷，且在某些业务案例中可能值得进行选择优化。
• shusaku赞同应考虑是否有更便宜的方式完成任务，例如使用硬编码逻辑，而不是依赖LLM做所有决策。
• crazylogger指出在复杂的实际代理流中，工具选择和参数传递是主要工作，省略中间的工具使用记录会导致代理失效。
• jaksa认为工具选择相对简单，但传递正确的参数是困难且容易出错的部分，智能代理应根据需要调整工具调用次数。
• bGl2YW5j认为问题不在于优化LLM的工具选择，而在于是否应由LLM来做工具选择，主张用硬编码规则和分离关注点来处理控制流。
• nphard85对viksit的方法在复杂代理工作流中的应用表示关注，询问其在多工具协调场景中的效果。
• digitcatphd认为NVIDIA关于微调小型语言模型的论文提出了更有效的方案。
• apsears强调LLM具有直觉，而自己拥有数据，适用于无法微调所用LLM的情况。
• tomlue建议将损失反向传播到工具本身。

补充讨论：
• 讨论的核心在于LLM在工具调用和上下文管理中的应用效率和优化方法。
• 争议焦点在于是否应由LLM承担工具选择和控制流的职责，以及使用较小LM进行优化的可行性。
• 不同参与者提供了各种优化方案和对比方法，如硬编码逻辑、损失反向传播和微调小型语言模型等。

data.title: Operators, Not Users and Programmers
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了消除“用户”和“程序员”之间区别的必要性，主张构建更具可塑性的软件系统，让普通用户也能轻松编程，而无需专门培训。文章以电子表格为例，强调其成功源于即时反馈和无缝部署。作者希望未来计算系统能兼具可塑性和技术稳定性，让编程像写简历一样简单。文中还探讨了现有可塑性系统，如WYSIWYG编辑器、浏览器开发工具和Sonic Pi等，指出它们提供了实时预览和无缝编辑功能，但缺乏如Git般复杂的版本控制。作者设想了一种无需事先批准即可使用和分享的系统，以增强用户的自主性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户与程序员之间的区别以及如何弥合这一差距，特别是在图形用户界面（GUI）和命令行界面（CLI）的环境中。

不同观点：
• jdp认为，CLI天然地将用户转变为程序员，因为每个命令都是可保存、修改和共享的程序。他质疑是否可以在GUI中实现类似的功能，例如命令历史的调用和修改。
• dustingetz引用Rich Hickey的观点，强调工具必须完全可被个人理解，才能激发创造力。他认为专家和初学者应使用相同工具，并将CLI与乐器类比。
• chubot支持将Unix shell演进为集成文本和图形的系统，认为文本界面不一定限于终端，并举例Excel和LibreCalc作为结合两种范式的例子。
• GianFabien指出，大型计算机公司倾向于迎合消费者而非程序员，通过消除易于访问的终端用户编程工具来实现，例如取消BASIC和HyperCard。
• rubyfan补充，企业环境中有意加剧这种分歧，IT部门通过控制用户可编程性来巩固管理角色。
• ppqqrr提到自己正在朝这一方向努力，并分享了一个相关链接。
• arduanika对这种方法表示赞赏，并期待看到更多发展。
• Jtsummers通过工作实例说明，允许终端用户自定义和修改系统可以促进协作，但需要合理的约束和保护措施。
• fellowniusmonk表示，个人项目可以很出色，但要使其生产就绪需要大量时间和资金。
• lmz认为，自动化有时是为了去除不可靠的人为因素。
• danparsonson强调，设计软件的困难在于处理每个决策的隐含意义，并指出并不是每个人都需要成为开发者。
• ginko对“消费者”这一标签持负面态度，认为无论是程序员还是用户，都应与计算机积极互动。
• michaelmrose进一步指出，人类的平均能力有限，开发易用软件并不意味着人人都会成为开发者。
• brundolf认为，AI可能是实现用户与程序员统一的最终途径，并指出这是计算历史的长期趋势。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应通过工具统一用户和程序员，以及如何在易用性和功能性之间取得平衡。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于企业控制与用户自主权之间的张力，特别是在自定义和修改系统方面。
• AI作为潜在解决方案被提出，但也存在是否能真正实现的质疑。

44476166.article_content:
This post is part 0 of a multi-part series called
“the computer of the next 200 years”
.
the modern distinction between “programmers” and “users” is evil and destroys agency.
consider how the spreadsheets grow
🔗
spreadsheets are hugely successful. Felienne Hermans, who has spent her career studying spreadsheets,
attributes this success
to "
their immediate feedback system and their continuous deployment model
": the spreadsheet shows you its result as soon as you open it, and it requires no steps to run other than to install Excel and double-click the file.
Rik calls Excel “malleable software” and the resulting programs
“vine-like systems”
:
The dream of malleable software is that we can enlarge the space of possibilities, users can enjoy more freedom and get more out of their software, without having to rely on software developers to provide it for them.
i would go one step further: the dream of malleable software is to unify users and programmers, such that there are just “operators” of a computer, and “writing a program” doesn’t sound any harder than “writing a resume”:
the distinction between "user" and "programmer" is an artifact of our presently barely-programmable and barely-usable computing systems.  I would like to use the neutral word "operator" instead.
—
Stanislav
this is a relatively new distinction! if we look at the history of computing and of programming languages, we see very different patterns:
In the 1960’s the supply of programmers was not very deep so IBM and other companies trying to gain a computer sale would often have to sell the business prospect on the idea of creating its own programmer(s). Sometimes it was the shipping clerk; sometimes it was the head order taker; sometimes it was a bookkeeper, and sometimes it was a woman or man packing items in the warehouse.
—
Brian M. Kelly, The AS/400 and IBM i RPG Programming Guide
this is what i want: for programming to be easy and simple enough to pick up that people can do it without specialized training in the field, so that they can write
situated software
.
the “user/programmer” distinction
🔗
contrast malleable software to the systems that programmers often build:
Many, many technologists have taken one look at an existing workflow of spreadsheets, reacted with performative disgust, and proposed the trifecta of microservices, Kubernetes and something called a "service mesh".
This kind of Big Enterprise technology however takes away that basic agency of those Excel users, who no longer understand the business process they run and now have to negotiate with
ludicrous technology dweebs
for each software change. The previous pliability of the spreadsheets has been completely lost.
—
Cal Peterson
now, this doesn’t happen because programmers are stupid and evil. it happens because the systems we build are amenable to all the features that programmers
take for granted
:
distributed version control systems (VCS)
automated testing (when integrated with a VCS, often called "continuous integration")
gradual controlled rollouts (when integrated with a VCS, often called "continuous deployment")
what i want to imagine is what it would look like to build computing systems that have those features and are also malleable.
what could a malleable system with
low technical risk
look like?
🔗
let's start by looking at what malleable systems already exist.
malleable languages
🔗
spreadsheets, as previously discussed
WYSIWYG editors: Microsoft Word, Obsidian, Typst, Wordpress. In Word, and in Obsidian's default view, the compile step is completely hidden and it appears to the user as if the source and rendered view are the same. in other editors, the rendered view updates quickly and frequently enough that they get immediate feedback, just like a spreadsheet.

, where editing code live-updates the sound played
my blog

data.title: Eastern Baltic cod grow much smaller than they did due to overfishing
data.author: littlexsparkee
data.article_summary: 一项发表在《Science Advances》上的研究揭示，波罗的海东部鳕鱼因数十年过度捕捞而发生进化，体型显著缩小。过去，这些鳕鱼能长到超过三英尺长，但到2019年，它们的体型缩减了一半以上。研究分析了1996年至2019年间的152个鳕鱼耳石和DNA，发现与大体型相关的基因变异逐渐减少，表明过度捕捞改变了鳕鱼种群的遗传构成。尽管海洋温度升高也可能影响体型，但进化改变主要是人类活动所致。这种变化可能使物种更难适应未来环境变化，恢复需要很长时间，甚至可能无法实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕捕捞小鱼对基因库的影响及相关生态问题

不同观点：
• ryao：认为放生小鱼以期望其长大可能会让“成年矮鱼”继续繁殖，从而损害基因库，建议这一发现应影响渔业保护规则。
• olelele：指出波罗的海因农业化学物质的污染，鱼类体内含有重金属和毒素，瑞典当局建议限制食用，特别是对孕妇和有健康问题的人。
• rr808：提到毛利渔民曾选择捕捞中等大小的鱼，留下最大的鱼作为最佳繁殖者，认为这种做法有其合理性。
• sharpshadow：通过无牙象的例子，暗示人类干预可能导致物种特征的变化。
• yard2010：表达了对蚊子进化的担忧，认为超蚊子的出现可能对人类构成更大威胁，甚至超过其他环境灾难。
• skeledrew：不同意将鱼变小描述为主动行为，认为这是达尔文生存选择的结果，小鱼因能逃脱渔网而存活并繁殖。
• weregiraffe：质疑按重量捕捞时鱼的大小是否重要，认为一吨小鱼和大鱼的重量是一样的。
• jongjong：指出进化可以在几代内迅速发生，人类捕捞行为可能导致物种特征的快速变化。
• thaumasiotes：提出传统解决方案是捕捞雄鱼而释放雌鱼，以避免雌鱼被排除出繁殖群体，但可能导致雄鱼进化得更像雌鱼。
• gouthamve：推荐了一本关于鳕鱼捕捞的书，讨论了人类活动对鳕鱼数量的影响。
• ivanbalepin：提到有人收集波罗的海鳕鱼的耳石，期待未来有新的用途。
• macinjosh：询问是否有“传统”鳕鱼被圈养或DNA样本保存，建议通过基因编辑技术恢复基因库。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到波罗的海污染对鱼类和生态的影响，以及对人类健康的潜在威胁。
• 对进化速度和人类干预生态的潜在后果进行了探讨，包括对蚊子进化成“超级蚊子”的担忧。
• 提到技术如基因编辑在恢复物种基因库中的潜在应用。
• 部分评论提供了外部资源链接（如书和文章），为深入了解相关主题提供了参考。

44474759.article_content:
A catch of Baltic Sea cod in 1987 shows fish that grew more than three feet long, with Finnish fisheries biologist Eero Kalevi Aro.
Jesper Bay of the Danish Institute for Fisheries and Marine Research, March 1987
A new study reveals that decades of overfishing have altered the evolution of cod in the eastern Baltic Sea.
The research, published in the journal
Science Advances
on June 25, aimed to answer a question that had puzzled scientists for decades: What’s behind the dramatic size change in eastern Baltic cod?
Study lead author Kwi Young Han holds a fully grown cod in two hands.
Thorsten Reusch, GEOMAR
These fish used to be enormous. In 1996, the biggest Baltic cod grew more than three feet long. By 2019, however, their sizes had been cut in half, and the cod’s weight was but a fraction of its previous glory. Now, the average cod can sit in a person’s cupped hands.
For decades, fishers in the Baltic Sea caught cod relentlessly, using large nets. Smaller fish could escape more easily, presenting an external pressure to remain smaller. But directly connecting the population’s decrease in size to evolution—and not other environmental factors, such as pollution or temperature change—is notoriously difficult for scientists.
Regulators banned fishing of eastern Baltic cod in 2019 due to a population collapse, but their size still shows no signs of bouncing back. In the new study, scientists find that overfishing did not merely remove the biggest individuals—it changed the genetic composition of the cod population, predisposing them to remain small.
“Human harvesting elicits the strongest selection pressures in nature,”
Thorsten Reusch
, a marine ecologist at the GEOMAR Helmholtz Center for Ocean Research Kiel in Germany and co-author of the paper, tells Emily Anthes of the
New York Times
. “It can be really fast that you see evolutionary change.”
Did you know? Shrinking body size
In animals, shrinking body size is a known response to warming, with populations of
birds, frogs and mammals
reportedly growing to smaller sizes over time as climate change raises temperatures. Individual clownfish have been found to
shrink during ocean heat waves
.
To uncover the reason behind the dramatic drop in cod size, researchers analyzed 152 fish otoliths—tiny, bone-like structures found in the inner ear—that were collected from eastern Baltic cod harvested between 1996 and 2019. Otoliths can act as records of a fish’s annual growth, serving as biological timekeepers, like tree rings.
The researchers then sequenced the DNA of each fish and searched for areas of the genome and genetic variants that were associated with the growth rate. In the end, the team revealed that over time, variants related to a larger body size had become less common. This suggests an external pressure was guiding the cod’s evolution.
“What we are observing is evolution in action, driven by human activity,” Reusch tells the
Guardian
’s Hannah Devlin. “This is scientifically fascinating, but ecologically deeply concerning.”
Though warming ocean temperatures may also be a factor in driving smaller cod sizes, the dramatic decrease in size is far greater than what scientists expect could have been caused by temperature shifts alone, according to the
New York Times
.
Scientists say that this evolutionary change in cod can carry consequences. The genetic variants associated with a faster growth rate might already be lost from the population, according to a
statement
. This decrease in genetic diversity might make it harder for a species to adapt to environmental changes in the future.
“Evolutionary change unfolds over many generations,” says Reusch in the statement. “Recovery takes far longer than decline, and it may not even be possible.”
Stefano Mariani
, a marine biologist at Liverpool John Moores University in England who was not involved in the research, tells the
Guardian
the work is a “milestone” in showing that human activity can speed up evolution. This, he adds, highlights the importance of tracking not only a species’ numbers, but also its gene pool.

data.title: How to Network as an Introvert
data.author: agcat
data.article_summary: 这篇文章为内向者提供了有效的社交策略，帮助他们在活动中更好地建立联系。作者强调，内向者并非缺乏社交能力，而是需要适合自己的方法。准备阶段包括提前吃饭、穿戴一件易于引发话题的物品（“Whatzit”）、浏览新闻以备话题。进入活动时，通过暂停观察、保持开放的肢体姿势和延迟微笑来塑造良好的第一印象。开始对话时，避免肤浅的寒暄，使用“你大部分时间做什么？”等问题让对方敞开心扉。对话中，注意对方的小细节并适时回应。与主办方互动时，提供具体反馈并主动帮忙。离开时，有意识地道别，并在24小时内跟进联系，记录关键信息以便日后维护关系。最终，内向者无需强行改变自己，只需展示真实的自我即可成功社交。

• joshcsimmons指出文章混淆了内向性格与社交焦虑，并认为对于有社交焦虑的人，最好的方式是不要过分在意表现，而不是遵循一系列的仪式性行为。

• yason对文章中描述的社交活动本身感到反感，认为这样的活动和技巧都令人不适。
• konsalexee提供了跨文化比较，认为不同文化背景下的社交开场白有显著差异，强调了非工作相关话题的重要性。

44475537.article_content:
How to Network as an Introvert
05 Jul, 2025
Why I am writing this?
Sometimes I’d leave an event unsure if I connected with anyone—or if anyone noticed I was there. I’d show up, blend in, talk just enough, smile just enough, and then disappear. The next morning, I’d wonder if anyone even remembered I was there.
This is what
often happens to introverts trying to network
. It’s not that we lack social skills. It’s that we’re playing the game without a system that fits our wiring.
I’m writing this blog as a reminder — a checklist for myself or anyone who relates — for the next professional gathering, party, or group event. A guide on what I now plan to do differently, step by step.
Before we begin: credit to the book
How to Talk to Anyone
by Leil Lowndes, which gave me this structure.
Before the event: shrink the unknowns
Walking into a room is easier when your nervous system isn’t in overdrive. Start with basics.
Eat before you go
. Most events are light on food and heavy on overstimulation. Being full helps you stay present, not preoccupied.
Add one small item to what you're wearing
that gives others something to comment on. It’s called a “Whatzit.” A pin, a vintage shirt, a random book in your hand. People need an excuse to start a conversation—give them one.
Scan the news for 2 minutes
. You don’t need to be a genius, but it keeps you from blanking out when someone says, “Did you see what happened today?” This isn’t about having talking points. It’s about removing friction.
Lastly, go over the
Six-Point Party Checklist
: Who’s going? When do you want to arrive? What’s the vibe? Why are you attending? Where is it exactly? How are you getting back? These simple questions give structure to an evening that often feels like chaos.
The moment you enter: control your signal
The most overlooked part of networking is the
first 5 seconds
. People scan you quickly and assign a story. You can shape that story.
Stand still in the doorway.Look around. Not like you're lost—like you're assessing. This pause signals confidence. Then pick a group that feels open and approach. No rush.
Keep your body open
. Wrists visible, arms uncrossed. Your posture is your pitch. Shoulders back, chin level.
Make eye contact before you smile. Let there be a beat. Then let the smile arrive slowly. This “delayed warmth” makes your smile feel specific, not generic. It’s subtle, but people feel the difference.
Opening lines: skip the small talk trap
Most people hate starting conversations because they overthink the words. The truth is, words are secondary. Your tone, posture, and energy do most of the work.
Start with:
“How do you spend most of your time?” Not “What do you do?”
It opens people up beyond job titles.
Listen for what lights them up. Echo a few of their words back to them. If someone says they’re working on solar hardware, ask, “Solar hardware?”—then pause. It gives them space to explain, and shows you’re actually listening.
When they’re done, don’t jump in with your story. Wait. Let the silence breathe. If you share something in common, wait a beat before you say it. The delay makes it feel like insight, not interruption.
Mid-conversation: be the one who tracks
Keep track of the small things
. Their dog’s name. The town they just moved from. That one thing they said in passing.
If you’re in a group, use their own story to spotlight them. Say something like, “You have to tell everyone about that glacier trip.” That line alone can shift how they remember you. It shows that you’re paying attention—and willing to share the room.
If the conversation stalls, don’t panic. Repeat the last few words they said with a slight upward tone. It’s called “parroting,” and it gently invites them to keep going without forcing anything.If someone says, “Work’s been kind of chaotic lately,” you can just respond with, “Chaotic lately?”—and let them take it from there.
Engaging the host: go specific, not loud
Hosts are often moving fast. Don’t waste their time with “Great party.” Say something more vivid. “The lighting is perfect.” “Everyone feels relaxed.” It anchors your presence with detail.
Offer to help with something small
—refill ice, carry extra plates. Tiny acts give you visibility without performance.
Leaving well: be memorable, not dramatic
Don’t disappear. Say goodbye with intention. Use an uncommon adjective: “Had a remarkable time.” “Such a thoughtful gathering.” That small twist makes you stick.
If you connected with someone,
follow up within 24 hours
. Share an article, a meme, a line that ties back to your conversation. This isn’t networking. It’s reinforcement.
Write down what you remember
—glacier, dog name, their startup idea. Those notes are your memory system for real relationships.
Three weeks later, check in. It’s not needy. It’s respectful. Most people forget. You didn’t. That matters.
Closing thoughts
What i have learnt is that you don’t need to work the room or become someone you’re not. Most of the time, it’s enough to show u

data.title: Yet Another Zip Trick
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章（基于提供的标题和链接结构）似乎是一个网站的部分界面介绍。"Redeem items" 指可以兑换物品，"Profile" 指用户个人资料，"Settings" 是设置选项，"Log out" 表示登出，"Login" 表示登录。页面中还包含一个电子邮件联系方式 "contact@hexarcana.ch"。整体来看，这是HexArcana网站的用户界面概览，提供登录、个人设置、物品兑换及联系支持的功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ZIP文件设计及其安全问题，尤其是包含PDF或DOCX文件时可能带来的风险

不同观点：
• **socalgal2**：认为ZIP文件中存在未在目录（TOC）中引用的内联头是设计上的特性，而非缺陷。这种设计允许在不重写所有磁盘的情况下向多卷ZIP文件添加新版本的文件。任何读取TOC以外内容的ZIP阅读器都是无效的。

• **jonathanlydall**：认为在ZIP文件中包含PDF本身就是一个安全隐患，很少见到合法的使用场景，通常应高度怀疑。分享了在处理公司域名邮件时遇到的诈骗企图，尤其是带有.svg附件的邮件，并采取了拒绝所有来自外部源的.svg文件的措施。

• **wingmanjd**：提出DOCX文件类似于更改扩展名的ZIP文件，质疑这种技巧是否可以欺骗Microsoft Word。

• **soupfordummies**：虽然承认现实世界中的问题，但欣赏这种技术 exploit 的巧妙之处。

• **o11c**：认为这个问题早在十年前就已经众所周知，没有新意。

补充讨论：
- **ZIP文件设计的技术细节**：socalgal2详细解释了ZIP文件的设计初衷和历史背景，强调了TOC作为唯一真实来源的重要性。
- **安全问题和应对措施**：jonathanlydall通过实际工作中的例子强调了ZIP文件中包含特定类型文件的安全隐患，并提出了实际的应对策略（如拒绝某些类型的附件）。
- **对技术 exploit 的态度**：soupfordummies对 exploit 的技术巧妙性表示赞赏，而o11c则认为这种问题早已被认知，没有新意。

争议焦点：ZIP文件设计是否是导致安全问题的根本原因，以及如何有效防范利用这种设计进行的攻击。

data.title: On latency, measurement, and optimization in algorithmic trading systems
data.author: auc
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了算法交易系统中延迟的测量和优化挑战。在高频交易中，速度至关重要，工程师们竭尽全力优化代码和网络路径以减少执行时间。然而，测量程序的速度和实际延迟非常复杂，因为需要考虑多个层次的因素，甚至测量本身也会增加程序的开销，影响准确性。

文章通过Python伪代码示例，说明如何测量交易策略的延迟，从计算模型估值到发送订单的各个步骤。初步方法包括在关键函数周围添加计时器，但这种方法存在缺陷，比如未包含发送订单的时间、观测所有市场交易而非仅触发订单的交易等。此外，使用`datetime.now()`作为计时函数本身较慢，可能影响程序性能。改进方法是使用更精确的计时器如`time.perf_counter_ns()`，但仍未涵盖网络I/O等关键路径元素。

最终，文章强调要全面理解交易系统的延迟，必须追踪从网络数据包接收到订单发送的整个过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高频交易系统中代码性能的测量和优化

不同观点：
• alexpotato 分享了在过去工作中处理高频交易系统的延迟问题。他们依赖随机森林模型预测预期延迟，并通过多种特征来分析延迟变化的原因。然而，IEX交易所并不跟踪自己的延迟，只能依赖他们的数据，这增加了测量的不确定性。
   
• foobar10000 强调了在交易系统中需要多层次的精确测量，包括不同时间间隔的均值、中位数、百分位数等，并提到硬件和网络卡时间戳在测量中的重要性。

• tombert 讲述了在使用.NET的async monad进行高并发代码 benchmarking 时遇到的挑战，指出由于async操作的调度特性，微基准测试可能会被误导。

• weinzierl 认为代码的快速性需要精确测量，且单一测量结果不足取信。他建议多次测量以了解数据的变异性，并强调在比较代码版本时应进行统计分析，主张使用最小值而非均值作为比较标准。

• am17an 补充了测量发送订单时间和决策计算时间的重要性，并提到L1/L2交换机提供的timestamp功能可用于测量端到端延迟。

• omgtehlion 指出在高频交易中，通过网络光纤的输入输出测量时间是简单且不影响延迟的方法，且可以在生产环境中进行。

• nine_k 认为编写快速代码本身不难，但保持一致的高性能很难，关键在于测量，并建议在CI/CD流程中加入性能测试以快速检测性能下降。

• iammabd 提到多数人只为理想路径编写代码，而忽视在压力下的运行行为，强调了对运行时行为进行细致关注的重要性。

• Attummm 认为文章标题是点击诱饵，因为文章内容实际上说明了编写快速算法交易系统代码的困难性，并特别指出正确测量的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何准确测量和比较代码性能，尤其是在高频交易这样对延迟高度敏感的环境中。
• 讨论中多次提到测量的不确定性和复杂性，以及多次测量和统计分析的必要性。
• 不同参与者提供了多种技术和工具建议，如随机森林模型、硬件时间戳、L1/L2交换机测量等，显示了在实际操作中有多种方法可以应对测量挑战。

How fast is it really? On latency, measurement, and optimization in algorithmic trading systems
byÂ
Brett Harrison
Blog
"The speed of light sucks." - John Carmack
â
Software engineers within the world of low-latency automated trading (colloquially known as "high-frequency trading" or HFT) obsess over speed. From purchasing private bandwidth between microwave towers to analyzing x86 instructions from different compiler versions, those with experience in this industry have seen colossal time and expense committed to the problem of optimizing code and network paths for minimal execution times.
But how does one actually measure how fast a program is? To the uninitiated, it sounds like a simple task. However, there are many layers of complexity in measuring the true latency of a trading system, or even defining what to measure in the first place. Understanding latencies in algorithmic trading systems can present Heisenberg-esque dilemmas, where the more code you write to measure latency the more overhead you add to your program and therefore the more inaccurate your measurements become.
At Architect we have been using a combination techniques to measure the latency of various codepaths and processes that comprise our institutional trading technology suite. Let's explore some solutions to these problems.
--
Let's say you've written an algorithmic trading strategy. Your strategy reacts to market trades in an instrument, perhaps by computing a proprietary model valuation, and sends an order in that instrument provided certain conditions are met. You would like to measure the time that this reaction takes
in a reproducible way
, so that you can reduce the time as much as possible. Let's use Python-style pseudocode to describe the program (although in practice it is most common to use languages like, C, C++, and Rust where optimal program latencies are required):
â
def
on_market_trade
(
self, instrument, market_trade
):
model_value = self.compute_model_value(instrument, market_trade)
order = self.compute_order_decision(instrument, model_value)
if
order
is
not
None
:
self.send_order(order)
A reasonable place to start in understanding the latency of your critical codepath is to wrap timers around the functions doing the heavy lifting:
def
on_market_trade
(
self, instrument, market_trade
):
start_time = datetime.now()
model_value = self.compute_model_value(instrument, market_trade)
order = self.compute_order_decision(instrument, model_value)
end_time = datetime.now()
self.add_time_sample(end_time - start_time)
if
order
is
not
None
:
self.send_order(order)
The function
self.add_time_sample
would add the elapsed time to a histogram that you could print statistics for at the end of your programâs lifecycle, or on some regular basis based on time or number of samples observed.
There are many issues with the above approach:
It measures the time required to compute the order decision, but does not include the time it takes to send the actual order.
It observes computation time on every market trade, rather than just the trades that result in orders â this can bias results because the most interesting times to send orders may be the ones where your program is running the slowest due to volume of market events or other factors.
datetime.now()
itself is a slow, expensive function that can impact the runtime speed and memory profile of the code above, which adds up if your program is already operating on a microsecond-timescale. The typical way to fix this last issue is to use native performance counters that most programming language have primitives to access.
Hereâs a new code sample that attempts to fix the above:
def
on_market_trade
(
self, instrument, market_trade
):
start_time = time.perf_counter_ns()
model_value = self.compute_model_value(instrument, market_trade)
order = self.compute_order_decision(instrument, model_value)
if
order
is
not
None
:
self.send_order(order)
end_time = time.perf_counter_ns()
self.add_time_sample(end_time - start_time)
This is an improvement, but are we really getting at the full latency of the trading system? The above doesnât include significant elements of the critical path, including the time to parse the market trade update, or anything involving network I/O. Letâs take a step back and trace a market data update through the complete critical path of the
automated trading system (ATS)
:
Network packet containing the market trade hits the network card of the box where the ATS is running (sent from the exchange)
The packet is passed to the runtime of the ATS
The ATS parses the bytes of the packet to pull out necessary fields (such as trade price or trade size)
The ATS computes a model value and makes a decision to send an order
The internal memory representation of the order is converted to the protocol of the exchange that the order is being sent to
The ATS makes function calls to

• omgtehlion 指出在高频交易中，通过网络光纤的输入输出测量时间是简单且不影响延迟的方法，且可以在生产环境中进行。

• nine_k 认为编写快速代码本身不难，但保持一致的高性能很难，关键在于测量，并建议在CI/CD流程中加入性能测试以快速检测性能下降。

• iammabd 提到多数人只为理想路径编写代码，而忽视在压力下的运行行为，强调了对运行时行为进行细致关注的重要性。

• Attummm 认为文章标题是点击诱饵，因为文章内容实际上说明了编写快速算法交易系统代码的困难性，并特别指出正确测量的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何准确测量和比较代码性能，尤其是在高频交易这样对延迟高度敏感的环境中。
• 讨论中多次提到测量的不确定性和复杂性，以及多次测量和统计分析的必要性。
• 不同参与者提供了多种技术和工具建议，如随机森林模型、硬件时间戳、L1/L2交换机测量等，显示了在实际操作中有多种方法可以应对测量挑战。

data.title: ClojureScript from First Principles [video]
data.author: puredanger
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了与YouTube相关的多项信息和功能。内容包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻资讯、版权声明、联系方式、创作者相关信息、广告、开发者支持、服务条款、隐私政策、安全指南以及YouTube的运作方式和测试新功能的信息。此外，还提及了NFL Sunday Ticket服务，版权归2025年的Google LLC所有。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ClojureScript的优点、使用体验、技术挑战以及其生态的成熟度和发展前景。

不同观点：
• throwaway0123_5认为ClojureScript对于偶尔需要快速拼凑前端功能的人非常有用，能够利用React生态系统的同时避免使用XML-like的JSX，语言本身也让人愉快。
• refset强调了ClojureScript的技术成熟度和近年来不断增强的生态系统，尤其是自我托管编译的能力，并提到当前有其他工具如sci/scittle/cherry继续推动这一愿景。同时提到即将到来的Jank项目，认为现在是尝试Clojure的好时机。
• tekacs回忆了一次技术会议上的讨论，提到在生产环境中保留足够信息以便通过REPL调试的问题。虽然这个问题解决起来相当困难，但tekacs认为未来可能会有解决方案。
• drdunce表示虽然不常做客户端开发，但ClojureScript使得这一过程变得非常愉快，避免了原生JavaScript和复杂工具链的困扰，唯一遗憾的是ClojureScript并不太流行。
• yayitswei提到Hyperfiddle的Electric Clojure消除了客户端和服务器端的界限，大大简化了代码编写，并对此表示高度赞赏。
• amadeuspagel对VSCode中使用REPL控制浏览器的开发流程持怀疑态度，认为在浏览器和IDE之间切换的工作流程显得荒谬，尤其是当VSCode本身也是Electron应用时。
• chamomeal认为ClojureScript虽然看起来很现代，但其生态系统让人感到困惑，入门有一定难度。
• cjohnson318简单表达了对ClojureScript资料的需求。
• dzonga提出了Google Closure即将终止的问题，可能对ClojureScript产生影响。
• ingen0s则简单表示对ClojureScript的赞赏，但时间上有所滞后。

补充讨论：
• ClojureScript的技术成熟度和自我托管编译的历史发展是一个重要讨论点，尤其是对该技术栈未来发展的期待。
• 在生产环境中调试和REPL的使用是一个技术挑战，虽然目前解决起来困难，但有未来解决的可能性。
• 不同用户对ClojureScript的开发体验存在差异，有些人觉得非常愉快，而另一些人则觉得入门困难。
• Hyperfiddle的Electric Clojure被视为一个突破性的工具，能够极大简化全栈开发。
• Google Closure即将终止可能对ClojureScript产生的影响引发了关注。

data.title: Ask HN: Advice for Starting a Hacker Space?
data.author: pkdpic
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：创办和运营一个成功的 makerspace/hackerspace 所涉及的各个方面，包括组织、管理、财务、社区建设和潜在问题。

不同观点：
• dv35z 认为该书是创办 makerspace/hackerspace 的“黄金标准”，涵盖了工具组织、人员配置、标准操作程序、敏捷方法、创业、资金等多方面内容，并提供了书籍链接。
• bsenftner 根据创办和运营 Droplabs 的经验，强调需要将所有正式成员及其行为和财务义务书面化，包括惩罚措施，以应对不遵守规定的情况。此外，还需要明确组织决策过程以防止无休止的讨论。
• jerkstate 指出商业性质的 hackerspace 面临更多问题，建议专注于社区规模的小型 hackerspace，并提出了一系列实际操作建议，如责任豁免、项目设计和志愿者机会。
• mjsir911 强调“Just do it”的态度，建议先找到物理空间并开始聚会，通过口碑吸引合适的社区成员，同时分享了欧洲风格 hackerspace 的经验，并提到创办过程中的试错和乐趣。
• Tomte 提供了一个设计模式的链接，并提到“Tuesday Rule”作为一个有用的规则。
• CursedSilicon 提到了西雅图地区的两个 hackerspace，并强调维持积极氛围和将空间打造成“第三空间”的重要性。
• yummypaint 建议从电子废物回收商或垃圾填埋场获取免费或廉价的物品供孩子们拆解和再利用。
• threatofrain 认为如果只是一个车库里的计算机俱乐部，不需要太多规划，因为空间和组织复杂性有限。
• kulahan 建议与当地图书馆合作，捐赠主要工具以获取支持。
• mandeepj 指出需要大量资金购买设备，除非专注于非常具体的利基市场。
• MongooseStudios 表示对该想法的支持，没有具体建议。
• cranberryturkey 开玩笑说如果有资金，会买一个便宜的房子改造成 hackerspace。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个实际操作中的具体问题，如财务管理、成员行为规范、项目设计、社区合作和空间利用等。
• 争议的焦点在于商业性质和社区规模的 hackerspace 之间的差异，以及如何有效管理和维持一个积极的社区氛围。
• 不同建议提供了多种视角，从实际经验分享到具体操作指南，涵盖了创办和运营 hackerspace 的多个方面。

data.title: Volvo delivers 5,000th electric semi
data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: Volvo Trucks已悄然交付第5,000辆电动半挂卡车，自2019年推出首辆全电动卡车以来，其电动卡车已在50多个国家运行超过1.7亿公里，大幅减少二氧化碳和氮氧化物排放以及交通噪音。尽管特斯拉Semi频繁成为头条新闻，但目前上路的数量仅约140辆，而Volvo凭借更早的起步和广泛的市场部署，在欧洲电动重卡市场占据了47%的份额。Volvo的电动卡车系列包括多款车型，满足不同运输需求，且公司高管对未来增长充满信心。尽管特斯拉曾在其他领域超越老牌车企，但在电动卡车领域，Volvo已建立显著领先优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于电动卡车的可行性、优势及相关品牌的讨论

不同观点：
• [qwertox] 认为YouTube频道"Bruce Wilson"可能是一个Scania的营销噱头，展示了欧洲卡车在美国卡车司机中引起的惊讶反应，并质疑为什么沃尔沃和戴姆勒卡车没有做类似的事情。
• [audunw] 支持电动卡车，指出电动卡车在隧道中不易过热和起火，并且减少了对通风系统的需求，特别是在挪威，电动卡车还带来了噪音降低的好处。
• [zvr] 提到沃尔沃卡车和沃尔沃汽车是不同的公司，后者已被出售给中国吉利公司。
• [iluvfossilfuels] 讽刺地评论电动是一个触发全球技术左派的关键词。
• [louwrentius] 提到YouTube频道Electric Trucker展示了电动卡车在上坡时轻松超越柴油卡车的性能。
• [ashoeafoot] 对电动卡车在经济上的可行性表示惊讶，并支持吉利和沃尔沃的发展。
• [jekwoooooe] 简单指出特斯拉电动卡车尚未交付，质疑其实际交付能力。

44477331.article_content:
Commercial EVs
Electric Semi Truck
Volvo Trucks
Volvo delivers 5,000th electric semi with little fanfare, sending a BIG message
Jo Borrás
| Jun 29 2025 - 12:18 pm PT
117 Comments
With the Tesla Semi making headlines consistently since its first public appearance
waaay
back back in 2017, you might think they were some kind of market leaders. Meanwhile, Volvo Trucks has quietly delivered its 5,000th electric semi truck … and they’re just getting started.
Volvo delivered its first all electric semi truck 2019. Since then,
Volvo customers in more than 50 countries around the world have logged more than 100
million
miles
(170 million km –
and almost half of that in the last 14 months as the size of its deployed fleet grows
) in real-world commercial operations, eliminating massive amounts of CO
2
and NOx emissions and reducing traffic noise. All the while, they’re making life a little cleaner and quieter for the people who live and work near the roads they travel.
They’re massive achievements, and Volvo Truck executives are very rightly proud of themselves for making them happen.
“It’s rewarding to see that transport companies continue to embrace the benefits with electric trucks in a wide range of transport segments,” offers Roger Alm, President Volvo Trucks. “Volvo’s battery-electric trucks are available here and now, providing our customers and transport buyers with a more sustainable alternative that makes business sense, and many of our customers are coming back to us to grow their electric fleets.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
King of the electric road
VNR Electric; via Volvo Trucks.
They say comparison is the thief of joy. That’s especially true if you suck and you compare yourself to people who are awesome –
and since Elon sucks like it’s his job
, I’m thieving a ton of joy by comparing the 140-odd number of Tesla Semi trucks out there to Volvo’s much larger, less-sucky 5,000-plus number.
With a head start like that, more than half a decade of production delays, and a “
dramatic
” price increase to something like $420,000 each, it seems like it would be tough for Tesla to catch up (
even if they
do
manage to begin series production in 2026
).
That seems especially true in Europe, where Volvo Trucks has established itself as the leader in the heavy electric truck segment for the last five consecutive years with a 47% market share – though the story is a bit different the US and Canada, however, where Volvo’s share of the electric truck segment was “just” 40% in 2024.
Volvo Trucks electric lineup
Volvo FL Electric
Volvo FE Electric
Volvo FM Electric
Volvo FM Low Entry
Volvo FMX Electric
Volvo FH Electric
Volvo FH Aero Electric
Volvo VNR Electric
Top comment by
Rob Guerney
Liked by 23 people
I really think the Tesla Semi, might have a major design flaw and might not be able to get enough weight on the steer axle and too much on the drives. Trucks have to make axle weight as well as gross weight, and i know electric trucks get an extra 2000 lbs. Tesla has a lot of empty space towards the front axle. Photos Initially show the frunk empty. Now they have moved the HVAC system to the frunk apparently to get some weight up there.  So I would guess the original design had no consideration of axle weight, which is a mistake legacy truck builders wouldn't make because on diesel trucks they  place the fuel tanks and batteries to get proper weight distribution. It depends on how far Tesla can move the batteries forward but the walk in cab might prevent that. In the the drawings with a see-through cab it looks like the batteries are forward, but it also looks like the batteries are where the walk in door us supposed to be. Diesels obviously have the weight of the engine up there Just look at a European Cabovers to see how much they put ahead of the front axle, this helps get the weight up. I'm guessing Tesla went for the "Wouldn't it be neat to have a walk in cab" look as opposed to the considerations of the real world of trucking. Of course all this is a guess since Tesla won't release the weights.
View all comments
That said, Tesla has beaten legacy brands with massive, seemingly insurmountable leads before – but the good news is that,
when it comes to EVs
, whoever wins, we kind of all win, you know? Even Elon! That’s my take, anyway. Head down to the comments and let me know yours.

data.title: July 5, 1687: When Newton explained why you don't float away
data.author: TMEHpodcast
data.article_summary: 《宇宙变得有序的那一天（ mostly ）》讲述了牛顿在1687年7月5日发表了《自然哲学的数学原理》，解释了宇宙为何保持有序，包括苹果为何落地、行星为何不偏离轨道等现象。这本书差点未能出版，幸亏天文学家哈雷资助了印刷。自那以来，牛顿的理论被用于建造桥梁、计算行星轨道以及解释日常生活现象，如烤面包总是黄油面朝下着地。NASA至今仍使用牛顿的框架发射卫星和进行太空任务。牛顿的定律为我们提供了一个大致可预测的宇宙，使许多现代科技成为可能，尽管物理学生在考试时可能仍会抱怨他的理论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《原理》及其相关科学概念和历史背景的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• dr_dshiv 认为牛顿在《原理》附录的最后一段描述了电磁学和电振荡在神经系统中的作用，并将其与“振动”（vibes）的历史联系起来。他引用了牛顿的原文，指出牛顿描述了一种最微妙的“灵气”，并讨论了这种“灵气”在感觉和运动中的作用。
• tristramb 分享了个人经历，提到曾对Paul C. W. Davies的著作持有怀疑态度，但后来在阅读其著作《第五奇迹》后改变了看法。
• progre 提到《原理》由哈雷资助出版，因为皇家学会因之前出版的《鱼类史》失败而缺乏资金。并指出哈雷自己后来也因学会没钱而未得到报酬。
• roenxi 认为牛顿的贡献在于精确描述物体如何下落及其计算方法，而不是简单地说“物体因为它们确实下落”。
• Simon_O_Rourke 幽默地指出牛顿没有解释像Joseph of Cupertino这样的特例。
• Liftyee 对网页上动画圆点跟随鼠标移动感到分心和不安。
• mattmaroon 提到牛顿的理论在现代仍有广泛应用，如建造桥梁和NASA使用牛顿框架发射航天器，但也调侃说“应该告诉他们相对论”。
• jrowen 纠正时间计算错误，指出《原理》出版338年，而不是337年，并提到自己出生在《原理》出版300周年时。
• tiahura 引用牛顿的名言“Hypotheses non fingo”（我不构想假说），认为牛顿回避了对“为什么”的解释。
• d4rkn0d3z 认为牛顿在概念上错误，虽然其工作在精确性上有价值，但时间并不“不可改变地从一个时刻流向下一个时刻”，也没有“神秘地作用于距离的引力”。他强调科学回答“如何”而不是“为什么”。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到牛顿的科学贡献、其理论的局限性以及现代科学的补充和修正。
• 争议的焦点包括牛顿是否解释了物体的下落原因以及其理论在现代科学中的地位和应用价值。
• 个人经历和对网页设计的主观感受也成为讨论的一部分，显示出讨论的多样性。

44477768.article_content:
The Day the Universe Got Organised (Mostly)
People were worried, mostly about everything, but particularly about why things stayed on the ground. Apples fell. Horses galloped. Cannonballs soared (briefly) and came crashing down. But no one was quite sure why the moon didn’t join in and plummet to Earth in the same enthusiastic fashion.
And then on
July 5, 1687
, Isaac Newton published a book with a title so long it felt like a Latin riddle:
Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica.
In three volumes, Newton calmly explained how the universe kept its house in order. Why apples fall, why planets don’t wander off, and why we aren’t all quietly drifting into space every time we sneeze.
It Almost Didn’t Happen
The Principia might never have seen the light of day if not for Edmund Halley—the comet chap—who personally bankrolled the printing. Newton, brilliant as he was, had managed to fall out with the only other mathematician capable of understanding him. (This was the 17th-century version of crowdfunding, only with fewer emails and more quills.)
Halley’s intervention saved science from being reduced to “things fall down because they do” for another century.
How We’ve Used It Ever Since
In the 337 years since, Newton’s ideas have been used for all sorts of fussy yet vital activities: building bridges that don’t collapse, plotting planetary orbits, and explaining why toast inevitably lands butter-side down.
NASA still uses Newton’s framework today. They strap adventurous humans into enormous cylinders, set off controlled explosions underneath, and fling them into space—because three centuries later, it’s still the best idea we’ve got.
Why It Matters (Even if You Don’t Think It Does)
We treat the Principia as a sacred text, but it’s really just a rulebook for how objects behave. Big ones, like moons and planets. And small ones, like apples, cannonballs, and the pen you dropped under the fridge last week.
Newton’s laws gave us a universe that made sense—mostly. They made possible everything from satellite launches to the quiet reassurance that, barring catastrophe, your kettle isn’t going anywhere.
337 Years of Falling Down Correctly
Today, we celebrate 337 years of objects falling over in a way we can more or less predict. Physics students may still curse Newton’s name during exams, but the rest of us can be quietly grateful he wrote down the fine print of reality so we didn’t have to.
Fancy more tales of science, silliness, and improbable feats of human ingenuity?
Tune into
The Multiverse Employee Handbook
—the only podcast that treats Newtonian physics like a bureaucratic policy memo with optional tea breaks.
🎧 Listen here
and let us help you understand why the universe isn’t floating off into a filing cabinet marked “To Be Sorted Later.”

data.title: Game publishers respond to Stop Killing Games claim it curtails developer choice
data.author: riffraff
data.article_summary: "Stop Killing Games"运动在欧盟达到重要里程碑，成为欧洲公民倡议，但游戏行业组织Video Games Europe表示反对。该组织认为，停止在线服务是多方面考虑的结果，当游戏不再具有商业可行性时，公司有权选择关闭服务。私服并非可行替代方案，因其缺乏玩家数据保护和内容审核，且许多游戏设计为仅在线运行，关闭服务可降低开发成本。然而，"Stop Killing Games"主张玩家购买的游戏不应因停服而无法游玩，认为这是计划报废行为，且其合法性在多国未经检验。该运动在欧盟已获超过百万签名支持，但即便成功，政策变化仅适用于欧盟地区。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：视频游戏行业中的在线服务、游戏下架以及玩家权益保护问题

不同观点：
• gryn认为，许多游戏设计为在线专用，但开发者不应将单人游戏强制在线，且应更透明地说明游戏为租赁性质，而非购买。同时，他呼吁玩家继续支持相关请愿。
• calibas指出，游戏发行商倾向于让玩家不断购买新游戏和内容，而不是开发像Terraria那样耐玩的游戏，目的是通过多次消费获利。
• hmry质疑游戏公司对私人服务器的担忧，认为如果游戏下架，公司不应为社区托管服务器上的内容负责，且玩家自主的服务器能避免公司对内容的控制。
• bellgrove以在Ubisoft工作的经历为例，批评公司强推Ubisoft Connect整合，且游戏设计缺乏创新，仅为时间消耗品。
• perching_aix怀疑“在线专用游戏成本过高”的说法，认为这种论点站不住脚。
• throw10920担心立法过程中的实际条文可能偏离初衷，导致不良后果，如过度监管、不公平负担或技术性错误。
• xg15认为即便当前议会可能不会支持该倡议，但讨论本身已经是一种胜利，迫使公司回应相关问题。
• pjmlp认为公司关心的是知识产权的再包装和复刻，而非让玩家自由访问原版游戏。
• chithanh建议开发者可以选择订阅模式而非单次购买，这样可以让玩家清楚自己购买的是长期服务还是永久游戏。
• umvi主张通过市场选择来避免不良商业行为，认为仍有大量不采用“阴暗手段”的游戏。
• LocalH强烈反对开发商随意下架游戏，认为这相当于剥夺玩家对已购买内容的访问权，类似于版权过期作品应进入公共领域。
• jimmydddd认为只需在购买时明确说明游戏可能在未来下架，即可满足“停止下架游戏”倡议的要求，无需复杂化讨论。
• PoshBreeze批评游戏公司对私人服务器的责任推脱，认为公司不应干涉玩家自主运行的服务器，且反对将开发单人模式与在线服务混为一谈。
• surgical_fire支持“停止下架游戏”倡议，认为公司应提供玩家继续玩下架游戏的途径，如开源服务器代码，并谴责公司通过租赁模式获利的行为。
• layer8预测立法若通过，只会将“购买”变为“终身订阅”，并不能真正阻止游戏下架问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于游戏是否应永久可玩、开发者是否有权下架游戏、以及如何在立法中平衡玩家与开发商的权益。
• 讨论中多次提到私人服务器的可行性与法律责任问题。
• 玩家与游戏公司之间的利益冲突明显，特别是在游戏下架与持续访问权方面。

44478083.article_content:
(Image credit: Westend61 via Getty)
This weekend, the Stop Killing Games movement
reached a critical milestone
to become a European Citizens' Initiative, but not everyone is on board. Video Games Europe, a trade association representing game developers and publishers in the EU,
released a statement
on Friday pushing back against Stop Killing Games.
Video Games Europe said in its statement, "We appreciate the passion of our community; however, the decision to discontinue online services is multi-faceted, never taken lightly
and must be an option for companies when an online experience is no longer commercially viable. We understand that it can be disappointing for players but, when it does happen, the industry ensures that players are given fair notice of the prospective changes in compliance with local consumer protection laws."
"Private servers are not always a viable alternative option for players as the protections we put in place to secure players’ data, remove illegal content, and combat unsafe community content would not exist and would leave rights holders liable. In addition, many titles are designed from the ground-up to be online-only; in effect, these proposals would curtail developer choice by making these video games prohibitively expensive to create."
Related articles
The 'Stop Killing Games' initiative is close to its final deadline, and after that, its leader is understandably done: 'Either the frog hops out of the pot, or it's dead'
Stop Killing Games surges past its goals, but a possible signature spoofing campaign could cause trouble: 'This is not a Change.org petition. This is a government process'
Ubisoft's defense against The Crew lawsuit doubles down on a point we've heard many times before: You don't actually own your games
"We welcome the opportunity to discuss our position with policy makers and those who have led the European Citizens Initiative in the coming months."
Video Games Europe's case is that it can be too expensive for developers and publishers to offer private servers or single-player modes in games that lose online multiplayer support, and that open or fan-supported versions of these games could present legal liabilities for companies, particularly when it comes to cybersecurity and content moderation.
The other side of that coin, as the Stop Killing Games movement points out, is that players are paying for these games. They don't (usually) get their money back if the game is shut down, so they're effectively paying for a product that's taken away from them. Of course, developers and publishers will argue players aren't buying a product but a
license
to access a game, but that's not how many players look at it.
As the
official Stop Killing Games website
explains, "Stop Killing Games' is a consumer movement started to challenge the legality of publishers destroying video games they have sold to customers. An increasing number of video games are sold effectively as goods - with no stated expiration date⁠—but designed to be completely unplayable as soon as support from the publisher ends.
The biggest gaming news, reviews and hardware deals
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
"This practice is a form of planned obsolescence and is not only detrimental to customers, but makes preservation effectively impossible. Furthermore, the legality of this practice is largely untested in many countries."
Regardless of what Video Games Europe has to say on the movement, it's clearly gaining popularity with gamers after garnering over a million signatures for its EU petition. Unfortunately, even if the Stop Killing Games movement eventually succeeds in creating some sort of policy changes, they will only apply in the EU (and potentially the UK, as well), so publishers and developers may still be able to permanently shut down games in other parts of the world.

data.title: Take Two: Eshell
data.author: nanna
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了作者对Emacs中的Eshell从最初的失望到逐渐接受并喜爱的过程。作者早期期望Eshell像其他shell一样工作，但后来发现其独特之处。如今，Eshell已成为作者Emacs使用中不可或缺的一部分，尽管作者并不像过去使用传统shell那样频繁使用Eshell。

作者指出，许多以前用shell完成的文件管理任务，现在可以通过Emacs的Dired模式更优雅地完成，如批量重命名文件等操作。对于源代码管理，作者使用Magit和VC模式，比git命令行体验更好。运行Makefile和重复执行复杂命令则可以通过Emacs的compile模式实现。

Eshell的最大优势在于结合Elisp使用，使其成为一个强大的命令行工具，能够即兴使用Elisp函数。虽然掌握Elisp需要一定学习成本，但其带来的灵活性和能力是值得的。最终，Eshell更像是一个Elisp REPL，而非传统shell。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Eshell及Emacs相关工具的优缺点，以及它们与传统Unix shell的比较

不同观点：
• **支持Eshell的观点（ndegruchy, xenodium）**：
  - Eshell是Emacs和命令行工具的结合，特别适合在Emacs环境中处理命令输出。
  - 可以通过Eshell处理远程会话和文件，无需单独的SSH会话。
  - 当把Eshell当作Emacs模式来使用时，其功能和编辑器功能可以无缝结合，模糊了shell和编辑器的界限。

• **Dired和其他工具的偏好（networked）**：
  - Dired是处理文件管理的更优雅工具，相比传统shell方法更高效。
  - 提到`vidir`和`edir`工具用于重命名文件，显示出非Emacs工具也有其高效性。

• **对Elisp和Eshell的批评（triclops200, imiric）**：
  - Elisp作为shell替代语言过于复杂，缺乏对简单性和惯例的保留，尽管其扩展能力强。
  - 更偏好xon.sh这样结合了Unix哲学和库功能的工具，认为其提供了类似传统shell的扩展而非替代。
  - Eshell模仿POSIX shell但未遵循Emacs界面指南，破坏了两者的惯例。

• **对Unix哲学的坚持（imiric, unixhero）**：
  - 强调POSIX兼容shell的通用接口和可替换性，认为Emacs工具缺乏这种灵活性和一致性。
  - 对Emacs依赖一个程序处理多种任务的方式持保留态度，担心未来出现更好替代品时难以替换。

• **对Eshell和Emacs整体的复杂性不满（unixhero, log101）**：
  - 认为Emacs的学习曲线陡峭，功能过多导致学习负担。
  - 希望有一本专注于Emacs精华部分的书籍来简化学习过程。

• **对Eshell脱离Emacs的期望（cmrdporcupine）**：
  - 希望Eshell和Emacs的其他功能可以脱离Emacs环境，成为独立组件，以实现更灵活的工具使用方式。

补充讨论：
- Eshell的界面和操作方式导致用户期望与实际体验之间的差距，部分用户认为其宣传不当。
- 不同用户对工具的复杂性和可替换性有不同需求，反映了在效率工具选择上的多样性。

notes from /dev/null
by Charles Choi ìµë¯¼ì
Take Two: Eshell
30 Jun 2025  Charles Choi
This is a contribution to the
Emacs Carnival 2025-06: Take Two
collection of posts on Christian Tietzeâs blog.
My first take with
Eshell
many years back did not leave a good impression. My early expectations was that it should act like any other shell, only to be unpleasantly surprised by it. It took a long time for me to warm up to Eshell. Upon reflection, it was because I wasnât ready for it.
Now Eshell is an inseparable part of my Emacs experience. Paradoxically though, I find little occasion to use Eshell in the same way Iâve used shells in the past. Much of what I used to use the shell for, I do today with Emacs modes instead.
It was not always this way. Like so many users who started Unix computing in the 80âs, I started with the command line (for myself
ksh
and later
bash
), studiously internalizing command line tools and their arcane syntaxes to support file management, running programs, and systems administration. Overwhelmingly though, it was file management and running programs that I did through the command line.
For file management these days,
Dired
is my interface of choice. It is simply the more elegant tool for the job.
Case in point: renaming a bunch of files in a directory to arbitrary names. With a shell, my standard approach would have been to run some variant of
ls -1 > foo.sh
, edit
foo.sh
to insert
mv
on each line to a renamed target file,
chmod u+x foo.sh
to be executable, run
foo.sh
, delete
foo.sh
and call it a day.
With Dired, the above steps are replaced as such: make the buffer writable (via
Wdired
). Change the target filenames to a desired result, then commit the changes. This is even easier if there is a pattern you can use a regexp for. Unsurprisingly, all the basic file management operations that you would want are supported by Dired. Add
Casual Dired
to help make these operations discoverable and youâll soon consider how quaint using
mv
,
cp
,
rm
, and
ls
are.
Running a simple command on a file? Again, you can do that with Dired. Move the point to the Dired line containing the file. Type â!â and enter a command in the prompt. You can optionally reference the filename in the command with the â?â character if you want to redirect its output to a file (e.g.
cmd ? > outfile
).
Taking file management and running simple commands out of what you would use a shell for, whatâs left over? Source code management (SCM)?
Like for many others,
git
is my goto tool for SCM.  Much has been said about the terrible user experience of the
git
command line and for years I suffered with its design decisions. Thankfully for Emacs users, there is Magit and VC mode which both provide a saner experience for it.
Running a Makefile? Use Emacs
compile
, which provides command completion for the targets defined in the Makefile and error/warning navigation if needed. (Try out
Casual Make
for editing Makefiles in Emacs.)
Do you need to run a command with arcane arguments repeatedly? Again, Makefile +
compile
to the rescue where it can be used as a task runner for that command.
Need robust terminal emulation? Eshell will fail you here and you are likely better off using a dedicated terminal emulator app, separate from Emacs. That said, Iâve found the built-in
term
to be good enough for many curses-style utilities.
Mining data files with piped commands? Eshell is a power tool here: used wrongly and you could figuratively cut off a limb. But used cleverly, Eshell offers great value. More on this later.
So with all these use cases described, why even use Eshell?
Using Eshell becomes a win only if you know
Elisp
. With that, you can think of Eshell as an Elisp REPL that can secondarily act as a shell.
Letâs not mince words. For many users this is a high bar, as it takes into account
a lot
of prerequisite knowledge. That said, learning basic Elisp is trivial for readers already conversant with programming and manageable for those that arenât. Personally, I was very late (decades!) in taking the time to learn Elisp because I didnât see the reward in it and so, prioritized accordingly. That hesitancy turned out to be unfounded. Elisp is easy to learn and the reward (or punishment) for knowing it is having the ability to really
use
the full capabilities of Emacs. (Know Python? Hereâs a
cheatsheat for Elisp
that I wrote, hop in, the waterâs fineâ¦)
Once gained, bringing Elisp knowledge to using Eshell gives you a command line super power: the ability to improvise shell commands with Elisp functions.
Consider the following Eshell example where we wish to apply a command on a set of
png
files in a directory. Letâs start with a simple example that simply echoes filenames with suffix
.png
.
$
for
i
in
*.png
{
echo
$i
}
In Eshell, you can replace
echo $i
with an Elisp expression.
$
for
i
in
*.png
{
(
format
"%s"
i
)
}
You can also mix shell commands and Elisp via
dollar ($) expansion
. Note that

data.title: Development of a transputer ISA board
data.author: nanochess
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在1993-1996年间开发transputer软件的经历，以及近期用JavaScript编写transputer模拟器的过程。作者为了在PC上运行旧软件，设计了一个与Inmos B004兼容的ISA接口板，并从eBay购买了transputer板。作者详细描述了ISA板的设计和制作过程，包括使用TTL电路设计解码原理图、焊接组件时遇到的问题以及如何解决噪声问题。最终，作者成功运行了1993年的Pascal编译器和光线追踪软件。随后，作者学习了KiCAD 9设计软件，创建了新的原理图并尝试使用自动布线工具。尽管遇到一些困难，作者最终完成了ISA板的设计和制作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Toledo的PCB设计文章及相关技术选择的讨论，涉及具体元件选择、PCB设计工具的使用、Transputer架构的优势和限制，以及对传统技术的怀旧。

不同观点：
• Kragen对文章中使用74LS00系列而非74HCT00系列表示疑问，质疑这是出于怀旧还是实际需求，并探讨了TTL与TTL兼容的CMOS之间的差异。他提到不确定ISA是否需要TTL电平，并对元件选择表示好奇。
• MeteorMarc对Kragen提到的KiCAD中的自动布线功能表示感谢，并分享了手动布线的局限性，特别是在原理图需要更改时，手动布线的体验不如自动布线便捷。
• Librasteve讨论了Transputer架构（特别是occam编程语言）相对于现代CUDA和SIMD架构的优势，提出利用现代工艺可以制造出更高效的Transputer阵列，但指出热量问题是主要挑战。
• Taid9iK对Transputer和Occam技术表达了怀旧情绪，回忆了相关的编程结构如SEQ、PAR、CHAN等，并表示这些技术曾给他带来心灵上的平静。
• Webdevver则从怀旧角度提出希望恢复传统的CPU地址/数据总线设计，希望在现代PCI上实现类似功能，并表达了对通过低级编程控制硬件的兴趣。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于为何选择74LS00系列元件，Kragen认为可能是出于怀旧，而实际应用中74HCT00可能更合适。
• 讨论还涉及Transputer架构在现代工艺下的潜在性能优势，librasteve提出了非常具体的计算和预测，但同时承认热量管理是重大挑战。
• 怀旧情绪贯穿多个评论，taid9iK和webdevver都提到了对过去技术的怀念，尽管他们的具体关注点不同。

Development of a transputer ISA board
I developed software for transputers in the years 1993-1996. A few months ago, I wrote some articles about my experiences, and most recently I developed a
transputer emulator in Javascript
.
After my transputer emulator in Javascript was working, I got curious about running my software on a PC computer. I have several PC motherboards with ISA connectors, and I decided to build a card compatible with the Inmos B004 (a single board to test transputer processors). Out of curiosity, I decided for compatibility because I wanted to run the Inmos Occam compiler.
A quick look in eBay and I got two transputer boards (TRAMs) for $25 each one. Both based on the Inmos T805 transputer running at 30 mhz.
I got the port numbers for the board from
Geekdot
, and designed a decoder schematic based on TTL circuits.
My first schematic for the board.
The TRAM board contains the transputer and its memory. It is connected to the ISA board with an Inmos C011 chip that serializes and deserializes the communication link. This chip is accessed via the ports 0150H-0153H. My ISA board also provides a 5 mhz oscillator, two flip-flops to reset and analyse the transputer, and a tri-state gate to read the error status.
Ports of an Inmos B004 board
Offset
Field
0150H Read
Receive data
0151H Write
Send data
0152H Read
Receive status
0153H Read
Send status
0160H Write
Latch bit 0 = Direct to Reset
0161H Write
Latch bit 0 = Direct to Analyse
0160H Read
Bit 0 = Direct from notError
I required a single ISA board drilled for homebrew development. I was going to buy one board in eBay for $35 dollars shipped, but I considered it was way too expensive. After some searching, I found the PCBWay showcase, where this same board was available for sale. And better, I could get 5 boards of 10x10cm. for $25 dollars shipped.
The ISA board for homebrewing.
I got the board and I started to put sockets for the chips. It took me a while to get the oscillator working. Once it was generating the 5 mhz. clock, I wired everything step-by-step, testing as possible. I was so happy doing this, that I never noticed I built the components on the solder side. My first insertion on a PC motherboard killed two 74LS08 when I feed 12V+ through the chips, until I realized my board was backwards.
My board also has a lot of noise produced by the wiring. After adding some decoupling capacitors, I was able to run
my Pascal compiler and ray tracing software from 1993
.
The transputer board working with the ray tracer. Notice my wrong mounting side, and that I'm using an AMD K5 motherboard.
The ISA board I've built.
Going the PCB route
A few weeks later, I decided to learn a little about KiCAD 9, so I installed it on my Macbook Air. Having used OrCAD many years ago, and my own programs that I developed later (I need to write more about it), I recognized most of the tools, and fortunately for this article, KiCAD comes with a predesigned ISA bus component.
Once I put the ISA bus component on the sheet, I wondered if there was a 74LS245 in the library, and yes, so I started adding the components. I wired the pins. I also used the component designer to create the Inmos C011 chip, and the TRAM pinout.
In less than two hours I had a schematic for my transputer board. It looked good, and from some tutorials in Youtube I heard about a very easy path from schematic to printed circuit board, so I exported the netlist, solved some bugs, and then invoked the PCB program. I discovered that I was missing the footprint for the TRAM.
With the footprint designed, the components appeared almost magically in the workspace. And you only had to click and drag and drop the components to their place! This was heaven! I didn't found an autorouter, so I went ahead to draw some lines.
I had worked five hours already, and I was pretty bored because I had to redraw line after line to make space in the board, or basically every time some line crossed the wrong place and it blocked other lines. I had heard of an autorouter for KiCAD, but it required to install Java (I remember in the 2010s I avoided as possible the slow and weird Oracle's installer), but I couldn't find a way to tell KiCAD I had downloaded an autorouter.
It happens KiCAD has gone through so many iterations that there are tutorials since KiCAD 6. I was reading the information for the wrong version. In KiCAD 9 you only need to open the complements window from the initial startup window, select Freerouter, and you need also to install a more compact Java version called Eclipse Temurin.
The autorouter didn't worked in the first attempt, because my board outline was open somehow. After some work I was able to make the outline in a single polygon. I made sure the design rules check (DRC) were correct, with some further work going back to the schematic to tag the unused lines, and correct the voltage lines.

44458532.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在1993-1996年间开发transputer软件的经历，以及近期用JavaScript编写transputer模拟器的过程。作者为了在PC上运行旧软件，设计了一个与Inmos B004兼容的ISA接口板，并从eBay购买了transputer板。作者详细描述了ISA板的设计和制作过程，包括使用TTL电路设计解码原理图、焊接组件时遇到的问题以及如何解决噪声问题。最终，作者成功运行了1993年的Pascal编译器和光线追踪软件。随后，作者学习了KiCAD 9设计软件，创建了新的原理图并尝试使用自动布线工具。尽管遇到一些困难，作者最终完成了ISA板的设计和制作。
44458532.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Toledo的PCB设计文章及相关技术选择的讨论，涉及具体元件选择、PCB设计工具的使用、Transputer架构的优势和限制，以及对传统技术的怀旧。

不同观点：
• Kragen对文章中使用74LS00系列而非74HCT00系列表示疑问，质疑这是出于怀旧还是实际需求，并探讨了TTL与TTL兼容的CMOS之间的差异。他提到不确定ISA是否需要TTL电平，并对元件选择表示好奇。
• MeteorMarc对Kragen提到的KiCAD中的自动布线功能表示感谢，并分享了手动布线的局限性，特别是在原理图需要更改时，手动布线的体验不如自动布线便捷。
• Librasteve讨论了Transputer架构（特别是occam编程语言）相对于现代CUDA和SIMD架构的优势，提出利用现代工艺可以制造出更高效的Transputer阵列，但指出热量问题是主要挑战。
• Taid9iK对Transputer和Occam技术表达了怀旧情绪，回忆了相关的编程结构如SEQ、PAR、CHAN等，并表示这些技术曾给他带来心灵上的平静。
• Webdevver则从怀旧角度提出希望恢复传统的CPU地址/数据总线设计，希望在现代PCI上实现类似功能，并表达了对通过低级编程控制硬件的兴趣。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于为何选择74LS00系列元件，Kragen认为可能是出于怀旧，而实际应用中74HCT00可能更合适。
• 讨论还涉及Transputer架构在现代工艺下的潜在性能优势，librasteve提出了非常具体的计算和预测，但同时承认热量管理是重大挑战。
• 怀旧情绪贯穿多个评论，taid9iK和webdevver都提到了对过去技术的怀念，尽管他们的具体关注点不同。

data.title: Mirage: AI-native UGC game engine powered by real-time world model
data.author: zhitinghu
data.article_summary: Mirage是一款由AI驱动的实时生成游戏引擎，允许玩家通过自然语言、键盘或控制器输入，即时创建和修改游戏世界。与传统预设关卡的游戏不同，Mirage支持动态、互动和持续的游戏体验，玩家可以随时生成新的游戏内容，如城市小巷、载具或扩展城市天际线。该引擎突破了以往生成技术的限制，提供更高画质、更长互动体验，并且支持多种游戏类型，如《GTA》风格的《Urban Chaos》和《Forza Horizon》风格的《Coastal Drift》。Mirage标志着UGC 2.0时代的到来，玩家可以创造、演变和重塑独特的游戏体验，而不再受限于预设脚本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成游戏世界的现状与未来潜力

不同观点：
• Peritract：认为当前技术并没有真正的持久世界模型，声称其为“世界模型”言过其实，只是现有游戏的模糊复制品，尽管技术有趣，但宣传过度。
• ilaksh：持乐观态度，认为尽管目前技术不完善，但与过去视频生成模型的发展类似，随着更多训练和优化，未来可能实现通过提示生成游戏，类似于当前生成视频或代码的能力，甚至可能应用到生产力工具上。
• abrookewood：对UGC（用户生成内容）不了解，认为当前示例类似于AI生成的Quake demo，缺乏实际的世界，只是过去游戏的“幽灵”再现。
• motoxpro：从趣味性和新奇体验角度看待当前技术，认为虽然不符合传统游戏标准，但提供了独特的体验，有其价值。
• samrus：提出两个问题，一是缺乏内在逻辑一致性，难以达到如《Skyrim》或《New Vegas》的深度互动；二是数据同质化问题，担忧AI生成内容可能导致市场饱和，抑制原创游戏开发。
• gausswho：持怀疑态度，认为相关讨论多为炒作。
• bakugo：批评当前demo只是GTA IV游戏视频的拼接，缺乏真正的创新。
• lianhuiqin：对未来充满期待，想象一个每个人都能创造、游玩和分享自己游戏的未来。
• zhenwang9102：对技术方向感到兴奋，认为上传图片生成游戏世界类似于《Ready Player One》中的OASIS，尽管目前仍粗糙，但未来可期。
• joechenphd：分享具体示例，强调通过上传图片生成互动游戏世界的酷炫功能。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于当前AI生成游戏世界的真实性和潜力。一部分人认为技术尚不成熟，宣传过度，另一部分人则看好其未来发展，认为随着技术进步可能带来革命性变化。
• 数据同质化和市场饱和是另一个值得注意的讨论点，特别是对原创游戏开发的潜在影响。
• 不同评论者对新技术的趣味性和新奇体验有不同看法，有的重视其即时娱乐价值，有的则关注其长期影响和艺术深度。

Play Demo: Urban Chaos (GTA-style)
Play Demo: Coastal drift (Forza Horizon-style)
The future of gaming isn't built level by level by expert designers—it's imagined, generated, and played by
anyone, in real time.
Meet
Mirage
: the world's first real-time generative engine enabling live UGC gameplay through
state-of-the-art AI World Models. Built to support dynamic, interactive, and sustained gameplay, it enables
entire worlds to be generated and modified live—through natural language, keyboard, or controller input.
Mirage supports various genres, and today we are releasing two playable demos:
Urban
chaos (GTA-style)
and
Coastal drift (Forza Horizon-style)
—both are fully generated on the fly. These aren't scripted experiences; they're living,
playable simulations shaped in real time by each player.
Mirage sits at the cutting edge of AI. Compared to recent works, such as AI Doom and Genie from Google, AI
Minecraft from
Decart, and AI Quake II from Microsoft, Mirage offers several distinct advantages:
It enables user-generated content (UGC) through text input at any moment during gameplay-marking a
significant leap beyond previous world-model-based game generation approaches.
It produces more photorealistic visuals, moving beyond the pixelated or blocky styles in earlier
systems.
It supports much longer interactive experiences, with playable sequences extending beyond ten minutes.
While
Mirage still has its limitations—as you may notice in the demos—we're confident that as we continue to push the
frontiers of real-time generative technology, it will play a defining role in the future of gaming.
UGC 2.0: The Rise of Generative Play
Traditional games are pre-authored: the city is laid out, missions are scripted, and the experience is
ultimately finite. Mirage breaks this boundary by letting players create new experiences dynamically as they
play.
Using natural language, keyboard input, or controller actions, players will be able to request an alley to
escape through,
spawn a vehicle, or expand the city skyline on the fly. The game responds instantly, weaving these
user-generated elements seamlessly into the ongoing simulation. The world isn't just interactive—it's
co-evolving with the player.
Mirage can generate games in various genres—from racing to RPGs to platformers:
◀
▶
This is
UGC 2.0
:
Where anyone can generate their own games from just a text prompt
Where players create, evolve, and reshape the game live as they play
And where every experience is unique, dynamic, and never pre-scripted
Built on Next-Gen AI
Mirage is powered by cutting-edge World Model research, featuring a large-scale, transformer-based
autoregressive
diffusion model capable of generating controllable, high-fidelity video game sequences. This
technology
framework integrates several key innovations:
A Foundation Trained on Games
Mirage is built on a robust training foundation designed for understanding and generating rich gaming
experiences. This foundation begins with the large-scale collection of diverse game data from across the
internet—providing the breadth needed to capture a wide array of game mechanics and styles.
To complement this, we built a specialized data recording tool that captures high-quality, human-recorded
gameplay interactions. These curated sessions enrich the dataset with nuanced, high-fidelity examples crucial
for training a model to grasp intricate player behaviors and contextual game logic.
The collected and recorded data is then fed into a vertical training pipeline—a domain-specific training
approach focused on games. This allows the model to deeply internalize game world rules, systemic patterns,
and interactive dynamics.
The result is a model capable of generating coherent, realistic, and flexible game content, moving beyond the
constraints of traditional, pre-authored games.
Interactive Generation Meets Real-Time Control
Mirage redefines real-time interaction by integrating frame-level prompt processing into its core. This
enables players to input commands or prompts that are immediately interpreted in the context of ongoing
gameplay.
Playable anywhere via cloud gaming:
Dynamic Input System: Mirage processes player input—primarily via keyboard and text—with ultra-low latency
for near-instant response.
Real-Time Output: Visual updates are streamed back to the browser through a full-duplex communication
pipeline, where input and output flow in parallel, eliminating lag and ensuring fluid interaction.
Under the hood, Mirage is powered by a customized causal Transformer model, augmented with:
Specialized visual encoders
Revised positional encoding
A structure optimized for extended interactive sequences
Borrowing from both LLMs and diffusion models, Mirage supports coherent, high-quality content generation. We
applied an advanced distillation strategy to the diffusion component that ensures both speed and quality.
Players can reshape the environment at any time using natural language, triggering instant world up

主要讨论点：对某个硬件项目的技术实现和可行性的分析，包括FPGA的应用和SMD手工焊接的难度。

不同观点：
• [Neywiny的观点]：Neywiny认为在这个项目中使用FPGA是一个很好的选择。他建议FPGA可以通过PCIe接口实现160个UARTs，但质疑7系列FPGA的I/O能力，认为可能需要等待Spartan US+系列发布。同时，Neywiny对IO电平问题表示担忧，显示出对该方案的部分不确定性。

• [Rochus的观点]：Rochus关注的重点在手工焊接SMD元件的难度。他对项目中有人能够在如此大规模下手工焊接SMD元件表示惊叹，特别是还进行了电路板修正。Rochus称赞了此人的视力和手工的稳定性，强调了这一技术活的高要求。

补充讨论：
• Neywiny的评论中提到了FPGA型号的选择问题，尤其是对7系列FPGA的I/O能力表示怀疑，并提到了未来可能出现的Spartan US+系列。
• Rochus的评论则更侧重于实际操作中的技术难度，特别是手工焊接的精细程度和所需的技术水平。
• 争议焦点：Neywiny对于FPGA方案的可行性存在一定疑虑，特别是对I/O能力和电平问题的担忧，而Rochus的观点则没有涉及FPGA，而是集中在手工焊接的实际操作难度上。两者关注的重点不同，但都强调了该项目在技术实现上的挑战。

不同观点：
• Valve不应上市或改变现有领导层，以避免损害PC游戏生态。
  - 支持论据：Valve未上市，能专注于用户服务而非股东利益。若Gabe Newell离任或公司上市，PC游戏将面临重大问题。
  - 例子：其他公司以利润为导向，可能破坏PC游戏。

• Valve在PC游戏存亡之际拯救了该行业，而非仅仅利用时机推出Steam。
  - 支持论据：Valve在其他大公司转向主机时坚守PC平台，并通过SteamOS和开放计算保持PC游戏活力。
  - 对比：Microsoft等公司转向主机平台，削弱了PC游戏的潜力。

• Valve应扩展SteamOS以支持更多硬件，并提供更简便的Linux桌面环境。
  - 支持论据：Windows 10用户不愿升级，一个免费且功能齐全的Linux系统能吸引更多用户。

• Valve面临的真正威胁是Microsoft等公司在游戏订阅服务上的竞争。
  - 支持论据：PC Game Pass等服务提供了大量优质游戏，且价格低廉，可能削弱Steam的市场地位。

• Valve的垄断地位虽引发担忧，但其成功源于平台的优越性和用户体验。
  - 支持论据：尽管在PC游戏市场占主导地位，但用户仍可自由选择其他平台，Valve并未完全垄断市场。

  - 支持论据：Steam已有硬件产品线，如Steam Deck和VR设备，进一步扩展至多媒体领域可增强其市场地位。

• Valve是否应扩展业务至其他媒体内容，或保持专注于游戏领域。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件测试的价值、成本和方法

不同观点：
• cloogshicer认为，说“无法测试”实际上是在表达测试的成本高于收益，特别是在需要大规模重构且使系统更难理解的情况下。他不完全认同测试狂热者所说的“更可测试的系统总是更容易理解”，并指出有些情况值得权衡，但需要仔细考虑。
• j_w建议隔离“不可测试”的部分以增加可测试性，通过为不可测试部分编写接口并模拟它们，可以避免这些部分吞噬可测试功能。
• testthetest提到，随着AI的发展，单元测试的成本正在下降，AI工具可以自动生成测试，但同时软件复杂性增加，黑盒端到端测试比单元测试更能提供信心。
• devjab主张运行时断言比测试更好，因为它们在问题发生时处理问题，而不是试图预测潜在的失败。他认为随着解释型语言的流行，这种方法被遗忘，但希望看到更少的“开发者聚焦”的错误处理方式。
• webdevver以讽刺口吻表示客户就是用来测试的。
• diggan认为该讨论内容像是博客垃圾，实际内容在一个YouTube视频中。
• aspenmayer关注的是提交URL的karma分配问题，并提到之前的一个先例，对使用脚本提交内容的处理方式提出质疑。
• somewhereoutth提出一个简化的测试哲学：如果由机器使用的部分可以由机器测试，如果由人使用的部分必须由人测试。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于测试的成本与收益之间的权衡，特别是自动化测试（如单元测试）与手动测试（如端到端测试）的价值。
• 有人提到AI工具在自动生成测试方面的潜力，以及黑盒测试在复杂系统中的重要性。
• 另一个讨论点是关于运行时断言与传统测试方法的对比，以及如何在错误发生时处理问题而不是预测问题。
• 还有对社区karma分配机制的讨论，虽然与主要讨论点不完全相关，但引发了对公平性和透明度的思考。

data.title: New study offers clues about what makes someone cool
data.author: _tk_
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：酷的概念及其在社会中的表现和价值

不同观点：
• glimshe认为，酷的人与研究酷的人之间交集很少，暗示研究酷并不能让人变得酷。
• neuroplots指出，资源和机会往往流向最不需要它们的人，高社交地位来源于对他人无所求，酷的本质在于不在乎，因为永远不需要在乎。
• voiper1引用了一个对酷人的特质的描述，包括外向、享乐主义、权力、冒险、开放和自主。
• whall6认为，通过学术论文来研究如何变得酷本身就不酷。
• neom认为，酷的人通常能提供灵感或洞见，酷是一种 aspirational（令人向往的）特质，并且与文化修养有关，具体特质与 voiper1 的观点相符。他还提到酷在不同文化和行业中有不同的表现。
• chriscrisby以幽默的方式表达，不用看就知道内容是显而易见的。
• webdevver分享了个人经历，从认为编程能力酷到只关注金钱，暗示价值观的转变。
• jaybrendansmith强调谦逊是永远的酷，真正酷的人不需要谈论它。
• sitkack引用The Rock的话，认为人可以有趣或酷，但不能同时兼具。
• rriley将酷与一种地位柔术联系起来，认为越少需求，越多人想要你。
• BMc2020详细说明了酷人的特质，并提出酷在建立社会等级和改变社会文化实践及规范中的作用。
• tomcam以幽默方式回应，表示显然不需要点击链接就知道内容。

补充讨论：
- 酷的定义和特质在不同评论中有所不同，但普遍提到外向、自主、冒险等特质。
- 争议的焦点在于是否可以通过研究或努力变得酷，部分评论认为酷是一种自然特质，而不是通过学术或刻意追求获得的。
- 酷与社会地位和资源的关系也是讨论的一个重点，neuroplots和rriley都提到无所求与酷之间的联系。
- 幽默和自嘲在评论中也被用作讨论酷的一种方式，增加了讨论的趣味性。

data.title: Ask HN: What old or outdated software have you never found a replacement for?
data.author: prisenco
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对已停用或过时软件的怀念与不满，以及替代品的讨论

不同观点：
• [dradra67] 认为Apple Aperture停用对其造成很大影响，不再愿意使用专有软件管理数字收藏，目前使用DarkTable，但尚未完全替代Aperture。
• [kingkongjaffa] 怀念Command and Conquer游戏系列，特别是3 Tiberium Wars，认为其玩法（如基地建设、资源收集等）在现代没有替代品。
• [austin-cheney] 提到自己多年前停止维护的一个应用仍然有大量使用量，暗示一些老旧软件仍有实用价值。
• [mikewarot] 对Google接手后的Picassa不满，因其存在bug（随机交换面部标签）而无法使用。
• [EdwardCoffin] 提到一个已停用的电影联动应用Inception the App，展示了对独特软件消失的惋惜。
• [FerkiHN] 喜欢使用Open Office制作演示文稿，认为其无广告、无订阅且习惯使用，尽管有其他替代品。
• [aleksjess] 指出有许多库可以实现其所需功能，但这些库大多已不再更新。

补充讨论：
• [FrojoS] 怀念Skype的国际VoIP电话服务，认为其价格低廉。
• [Metalnem] 提到ClickRepair这个已停用的软件，提供档案链接。
• [j-krieger] 认为MacOS上缺乏能够有效调整不同应用音量的现代工具。
• [torunar] 提到X11这个图形用户界面标准，未具体评价。
• [delduca] 怀念Turbo C与conio.h，暗示对旧开发环境的怀念。
• [fat_cantor] 提到Dark Sky这个应用，未具体评价。
• [dogman1050] 认为Winamp的经典皮肤虽老但不过时，展示了对经典界面的喜爱。
• [lproven] 强调大纲工具对长篇写作的重要性，认为现代工具不如20-30年前的MS Word二进制文件有效，批评现代工具的简陋。

争议焦点：
• 专有软件停用对用户的影响与用户是否应再次投入精力使用新软件。
• 老旧软件的实用价值与现代替代品的不足。

总结：评论中用户普遍对已停用或过时的软件表示怀念，并对现代替代品表示不满，反映出对软件长期支持和替代方案的关注。

data.title: Get the location of the ISS using DNS
data.author: 8organicbits
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种通过DNS LOC记录来获取国际空间站（ISS）位置的有趣方法。作者利用了RFC 1876实验标准，该标准允许在DNS中存储服务器的经纬度和海拔信息。作者创建了一个域名“where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io”，并通过N2YO网站的API获取ISS的实时位置数据，将其转换为LOC记录格式，定期更新。该方法使用Linux和Mac系统的`dig`命令查询ISS位置，每15分钟更新一次记录。作者还介绍了如何使用deSEC的服务来添加和更新DNS LOC记录。这种方法展示了一种复杂而有趣的方式来利用DNS存储和分发 unlikely 的数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过DNS记录和API获取国际空间站（ISS）位置信息的技术方法及其局限性

不同观点：

• theobeers分享了通过DNS的NAPTR记录获取约翰逊航天中心电话号码的技术细节，提供了另一种获取相关信息的方式。

44480223.article_content:
I love DNS esoterica. Weird little things that you can shove in the global directory to be distributed around the world instantly(ish).
Domain names, like
www.example.com
usually resolve to servers. As much as we think of "the cloud" as being some intangible morass of ethereal Turing-machines floating in probability space, the more prosaic reality is that they're just boxen in data centres. They have a physical location.
Got a tricky machine which is playing silly-buggers? Wouldn't it be nice to know exactly where it is? That way you can visit and give it some
percussive maintenance
.
Enter the DNS LOC record!
The snappily titled
RFC 1876
is an
experimental
standard. It allows you to create a DNS record which specifies the latitude and longitude of your server. Of course, some data-centres are very tall and some are underground. So it also contains an altitude parameter.
The standard allows for a minimum altitude of -100,000 metres - deep enough for any bunker! The maximum altitude is 42,849,672 metres which is high enough to allow it to be used on
satellites in geostationary orbit
.
So, as a bit of fun, I decided to create
where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io
It isn't a website. You can't ping it. There's no way to interact with it
except
by using DNS.  Yup! You can use a DNS query to get the (approximate) location of the International Space Station!
Linux and Mac users
0
can run:
dig where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io LOC
And receive back the latest position of the ISS:
;; ANSWER SECTION:
where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io. 1066 IN  LOC 47 24 53.500 N 66 12 12.070 W 430520m 10000m 10000m 10000m
The DNS records are updated every 15 minutes on a best-effort basis
1
.
How
The lovely people at
N2YO
have a website which allows you to track
loads
of objects in orbit.  They also have an
easy to use API
with a generous free tier.
Calling
https://api.n2yo.com/rest/v1/satellite/positions/25544/0/0/0/1/&apiKey=_____
gets back the latest position:
JSON
{
"info"
:
{
"satname"
:
"SPACE STATION"
,
"satid"
: 25544,
"transactionscount"
: 7
}
,
"positions"
:
[
{
"satlatitude"
: -21.25409321,
"satlongitude"
: 140.3335763,
"sataltitude"
: 420.09,
"azimuth"
: 292.92,
"elevation"
: -70.95,
"ra"
: 202.69300845,
"dec"
: -32.16097472,
"timestamp"
: 1751366048,
"eclipsed"
: true
}
]
}
Note that the altitude is in Km, whereas the LOC format requires m.
The latitude and longitude are in decimal format - they need to be converted to Degrees, Minutes, and Seconds.
There were only a few free domain name providers who offer an API for updating LOC records.  I went for
deSEC
a charity from Berlin. They have
comprehensive API documentation
.
Adding the initial LOC record is done with:
Bash
curl https://desec.io/api/v1/domains/where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io/rrsets/ \
--header "Authorization: Token _______" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" --data @- <<< \
'{"type": "LOC", "records": ["40 16 25.712 S 29 32 36.243 W 427550m 0.00m 10000m 10m"], "ttl": 900}'
However, updating the record is a little trickier. it needs to be sent as an
HTTP PATCH
to a subtly different URl. The PATCH only needs to send the data which have changed.
Bash
curl -X PATCH https://desec.io/api/v1/domains/where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io/rrsets/@/LOC/ \
--header "Authorization: Token _______" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" --data @- <<< \
'{"records": ["40 16 25.712 S 29 32 36.243 W 427550m 0.00m 10000m 10m"]}'
I set the
Time To Live
at 900 seconds. Every 15 minutes my code runs to update the record
2
. That keeps me well within the API limits for both services.  I could add TXT records showing when it was last updated, or other sorts of unstructured data, but I think this is enough for a quick proof-of-concept.
There you have it! A complex and silly way to demonstrate how DNS can be used to hold the most unlikely of records
3
.  Say, I wonder how you'd represent the co-ordinates of the Mars Rover…?
Further Reading
For more DNS weirdness, please see my other posts:
BIMI - SVG in DNS TXT WTF?!
Why you can't dig Switzerland
I don't think there's a way for Windows users to look up LOC records using PowerShell or the Command Prompt.
↩︎
Look, I'm not NASA, OK? If you're using this to help you dock then I cannot be held responsible.
↩︎
I suppose you could build an API with unlimited request limits by distributing data via DNS TXT records. Would best suit static or infrequently updating data. Push it once to DNS and let everyone query it semi-locally.
↩︎
See if you can find the other interesting record I've added to DNS!
↩︎

data.title: The War on the Walkman
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 《The Forgotten War on the Walkman》一文回顾了1979年索尼Walkman面世后引发的争议。虽然Walkman如今被视为1980年代的象征，带来怀旧情感，但其诞生之初却遭遇不少批评。文化评论家认为Walkman加剧了个人主义，导致社会隔离，甚至有人将其比作“感官抑制剂”。批评者还担心Walkman影响驾驶和行人的安全，美国多个州因此立法限制使用头戴式耳机。新泽西州Woodbridge镇甚至禁止步行过街时佩戴Walkman耳机，违者可能面临罚款和监禁。一位抗议该法律的居民Oscar Gross虽有意上诉至最高法院，但在一名耳机佩戴者发生交通事故后放弃。文章提醒人们，新技术往往面临抵制，怀旧情绪常让人忘记曾经的争议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人音频技术（如耳机、无线耳机）对社交互动、音乐体验以及公共安全的影响

不同观点：
• **支持个人音频设备的观点**：  
  - [comrade1234] 认为流媒体和DJ的音乐策展提供了丰富的音乐选择，且没有必要回到过去"拥有"音乐的时代。人类策展的音乐比算法推荐的更具多样性。
  - [tempodox] 提出无线耳机的使用并没有导致社会崩溃，暗示对新技术的焦虑是过度夸大的。

• **反对个人音频设备的观点**：  
  - [Lio] 偏好戴耳机的人的安静，而不是播放低质量音乐或使用自动调音的视频内容的人制造的噪音，认为这种音乐令人不适。
  - [MarkusWandel] 指出智能手机和无线耳机的普及导致人们忽视周围环境，甚至在公共道路上不注意他人的存在，增加了危险。
  - [deadbabe] 批评现代社会对人的关心减少，变得更交易性，只在对自己有利时才表现出同情。

• **对新技术影响的反思**：  
  - [sevensor] 提出个人耳机可能导致人与人之间的疏远，使得与陌生人交谈变得更加困难，类似于社会疏离的表现。
  - [xg15] 承认新技术确实引发焦虑和社会变动，但质疑当前技术的 impact 是否与过去相同，认为需要更深入分析。

• **对公共安全的关注**：  
  - [gwern] 提到与耳机相关的公共安全事故，例如有人在过马路时因戴耳机而发生悲剧，指出这是自由的不可避免的代价。
  - [snozolli] 提到人们对事故受害者的指责现象，并将其归因于“公正世界谬误”和魔法思维，反映出对受害者听音乐行为的过度归因。

补充讨论：
- **怀旧情绪**：  
  - [jb1991] 和 [Nifty3929] 提到对过去技术使用的怀念，并暗示对当前技术的批评可能是暂时的，未来可能会看到不同的变化。

- **音乐体验的变化**：  
  - [relaxing] 提到过去使用卡带播放器是没有广告的用户自选内容体验，而今天的内容则更多由算法推荐，可能受到商业利益影响。

- **多任务处理与分心**：  
  - [tom89999] 指出智能手机导致更多分心，包括听音乐时被电话和社交媒体打断，认为这会影响人的专注力和社交质量。
